text:
aria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak from yesterday, we've got more long-request tail and short tenants are seeing better latency but long sequences get repeatedly deferred. Looks like continuous-batcher code is favoring kernels with lower per-token cost and that interacts badly with our slot allocator.

sam: ugh. can you paste a small repro + profile?

aria: repro is: run loadbench with mixed seq lengths (p95 len ~ 1600, p50 ~ 40) and tenant mix 60/40 long/short. Command: `./tooling/loadbench --config tests/mixed_long_short.yaml --qps 200`

mike: paste of perf sample (top of hot path):
```
# perf report snippet
samples: 12000
kernel_select()  42%   continuous_batcher.cpp:248
batch_assemble()  27%   queue_policy.cpp:89
kv_cache_lookup() 15%   kv_cache.cpp:132
rpc_send()        10%   outbound.cpp:54
```

leila: looks like kernel_select now biases long sequences into fast-quantized kernels which increase per-batch latency for short slots because of queuing. also kv_cache hit-rate dropped for long seqs (cold miss churn).

aria: exact symptom: queue depth for long-tenant lane grows and mini-batcher keeps coalescing them into large microbatches; that delays short requests waiting for a batch fill. short tenants get small latency wins but overall fairness degrades.

nora: any regressions in KV eviction telemetry?

aria: yes, kv eviction bump around the same time (earlier commits show steady hit-rate ~0.87, now down to 0.74 under mixed load). logs:
```
[2026-02-24T16:12:03Z] tenant=tenant-long kv_hit=false key=cache_key:....
[2026-02-24T16:12:03Z] tenant=tenant-long evicted=true reason=kv_pressure
```

sam: hypothesis: kernel-selection increases memory working set or changes access pattern so kv prefetch/warmup is less effective -> more misses -> longer inference path -> longer batch wait.

mike: quick mitigation idea: enforce short-slot reservation + cap per-tenant inflight tokens. i.e. token_budget_target per tenant = min(global_budget*weight, absolute_cap). For long tenants lower the aggressive fill target.

leila: we tried reserve slots before; it helps latency for shorts but reduces overall throughput. Need a tunable that smooths token credits rather than hard reserve. Suggest smoothing window on credit refill: low-pass filter credits so bursts don't instantly steal slots.

aria: propose experiment: introduce three knobs in canary config: `short_slot_reserve_pct`, `token_credit_smoothing_tau_sec`, `max_tokens_per_tenant_window`. Default: 0.08, 2.0, 8000.

nora: add metric `slot_starve_ratio{tenant}` to track fraction of short slots delayed >50ms due to waiting on long batch. Also `kv_rewarm_time` histogram.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: cid=ci-98231, target=canary-2, config=aria/shortslot-expt

sam: plan: A/B canary 25% -> 50% -> 100% if no regressions. Collect: p50/p95 latency per-tenant, kv_hit_rate, slot_starve_ratio, throughput delta. Rollback on any p95 regression >5% for short tenants or any drop in kv_hit_rate >0.06.

mike: also add microprobe in batcher: if head of queue is long and waiting >X ms and short exists behind it, allow preempt to pack short into existing GPU slot (preemptive latch). That requires kernel compatibility checks though.

leila: kernel compatibility is the blocker; some kernels require different tensor layouts. We can add a cheap fast-path: if kernel flags are compatible (same dtype/kv-layout) allow preemptive attach. Fallback: fall back to existing path.

aria: I ran a quick sim on local env with smoothing_tau=2 and short_slot_reserve=0.06: p95 short improved by 18%, long p95 increased 6%, throughput -1.4%. KV hit-rate recovered to 0.81. Simulation config + results attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/shortslot-sim-1

nora: good. please add a dashboard with these new metrics and an alert: slot_starve_ratio > 0.12 for >5m.

sam: doc action: write up canary checklist and experiment dashboard panels. I'll own rollout. aria you PR the config toggles + smoothing code. mike you prototype preemptive attach as opt-in flag behind runtime toggle. leila handle dashboard and add automated daily job to recompute optimal token_credit_target per workload using historical seq-length distribution.

aria: will open PR today with tests + smoke harness. quick note: add unit test for credit smoothing (simulate pulses and assert no >50% immediate credit jump).

mike: simple repro script in case folks want to rerun locally: `scripts/repro_long_short.sh --qps 200 --short-pct 40 --lengths 40,1600`

leila: tagging infra for canary: @infra-team pls spin canary-2 with config `shortslot-expt` when PR lands.

infra-bot: canary deployed: cid=ci-98231 -> canary-2 live (25%)

sam: cool. we monitor the dashboard for 2 hours then decide. thanks all :+1:

aria: thanks — will update here with PR link and initial telemetry snapshot.
